Retro nonsense, correctly applied

CV in a Box

A CV packaged like old software. Completely unnecessary, took far longer than writing a CV. I wanted to know whether something people pick up beats something people skim.

Video Artwork PDF
BUILD SPEC RUN OF ONE
Box format
Big-box PC game, the size software used to come in. Underneath it is a cereal box with printed panels glued on, then shrink-wrapped.
Artwork
Drawn in Inkscape, modelled on an old Windows 95 box. Open source tools for a box pretending to be shrink-wrapped commercial software.
Print process
Photo paper on a refillable-tank Canon inkjet, which is both cheaper and better than cartridges. Colours came out right first time.
Contents
The printed CV. Plus a fake serial number and a fake hologram seal (so you know it's real).
Print run
One.
Cost per box
Depends how much you value your time.

Did it work

The one box went to one company, registered post, and I never heard back. So: yes - I don't want to work for a company that wouldn't respond to this.

What I would change

It was a one-off and I am not sure I would repeat it. If I did, I would send more than one, and I would aim it at somewhere more likely to open the box.
